title: Paraclr: Paraclr replaces the liquidation race with a clock

lines.text: October twenty twenty-five. Crypto's largest liquidation day ever.
More than nineteen billion dollars. One point six million traders. In twenty-four hours.
Every one of those liquidations was a race. Bots bid gas to land first.
The winner takes a penalty that was fixed in advance. And the trader pays it, whatever the market was actually willing to take.
Paraclr replaces the race with a clock.
When an account goes underwater, it enters a Dutch auction. The discount starts at zero and rises five basis points every block. On Monad, that's a step every third of a second.
The backstop pool can take from seventy-five, about five seconds in. More gas only buys an earlier take, at a smaller discount.
Every account lives in one of eight lanes, each with its own storage. A crash in one lane never touches another. That's exactly the shape Monad's parallel execution rewards.
This is live on Monad testnet. Sign in with Privy, by passkey or email. No seed phrase.
Get gas from the drip, claim test AUSD from Agora's faucet, and open a long on SOL. The order fills at the first Pyth price after a short delay, so nobody picks their own price.
Now crash the market. Anyone can, in the Arena. One click drops prices twenty percent.
Each lane runs its own auctions, and the backstops take them, lane by lane, in seconds.
We measured a crash on Monad testnet. The auctions took twenty-eight percent less from traders than the fixed fee would have. Whatever the auction doesn't need goes back to the trader.
Then we traced every transaction. The same crash, on a build that keeps every total in one shared slot, created forty-nine dependencies across lanes.
Paraclr's lanes: zero. They never wait on each other.
Built on Monad. Agora AUSD as collateral, Pyth prices, Privy sign-in, Envio indexing every order and auction. Owned by a Safe behind a timelock. Tested hard. Not yet audited.
Paraclr. Fair liquidations for Monad. Crash it yourself, at paraclr dot x y z.
